content.rationale:
This decision models the registry side of `deccy discard` as Quint state: one call over the draft registry, in `specs/drafts/discard.qnt` (module `draft_discard`), in the house form of `specs/markers/state.qnt` and `specs/store_bulk/read.qnt` - a module that imports the state model and steps its variable, with the action as its only export. The check `specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt` (skvuyuyq) fixes the interface this module must carry - `action discard(handles: List[str])` over `records`, total over the handle list - and the module supplies exactly that action.

The four prerequisites license every part of it. slwvtspu fixes what a discard ends: an open draft, ended without landing, with no node and no change written. So the only subject a call can name is a record that is still `open`, and the action writes the registry and no other variable. lnpnkvkv fixes the selection and the refusal: the handles are that verb's only arguments and the only key that addresses a draft, one open draft per handle, and a call naming any handle that is not an open record is refused whole rather than answered in part, with a duplicate handle naming the same draft once and no node or change written. That is the module's one rule: `discardAccepted` holds exactly when every handle in the list picks out an `open` record of the registry as it stands, the handles are read as a set so repetition collapses and order carries nothing, and the refusal leaves `records` untouched. yomurusp fixes the store side read over the registry: exactly the named records' documents go, so an accepted call rebuilds the map with the named handles removed and every other record kept at its own handle; every other record stays at its handle, so no record is rewritten, renamed or moved and none is added; a landed record is never removed, which the subject rule makes structural - a `landed` record fails `discardSubject` and so refuses the whole call; and absence is no third state, so a removed record is simply absent from the map and no state value or transition is added for it. tvtnokzu fixes the record's form, its two states `open` and `landed`, and the registry map `records`; the module imports all of that from `draft_state` and restates none of it - no field, no constructor, no base, no transition of the record is defined here.

The action is total over the handle list it is given and has exactly two outcomes, never a third. An accepted call steps `records` to exactly the records it did not name; a refused call steps `records` to itself. There is no precondition that could disable the action and no partial application: an empty list names no handle, so it is vacuously accepted and removes nothing, and a list mixing an open handle with a landed or absent one is refused whole so that the open draft it named is still there. Because the effect is one assignment of one variable, the model states no output, no wording, no stream and no exit status, and no other part of the invocation.

The change abandonment and the workspace forget a real discard performs are jj and filesystem effects and are deliberately outside this model: `discard` abandons no change, forgets no workspace, touches no path, and the module states nothing about either. Also outside, because each is another decision and none of them is needed to state this one: the record document's removal at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` as a filesystem act (the registry's removal is the model's stand-in for it, not a claim about the path), how a handle is minted, and the verb surface that slwvtspu and lnpnkvkv already fix.

The module is carried as Quint because the house checks decisions of this kind by running them: the record shape and the lifecycle are already a machine artifact (tvtnokzu), and a discard that must be total, exact and whole-call-refusing across a handle list is a property of a transition relation, not of prose. `specs/drafts/discard_check.qnt` composes this action into a step and runs it against a seeded registry, which is the form the house uses for a model it intends to model-check.
